newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary FX futures dealers close short positions.
newsitem.headline: Hungary FX futures dealers close short positions.

text.p: Hungary's currency futures market saw above-average turnover on Monday as traders closed their March positions, dealers said.

The Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) saw 6.48 billion forints' turnover, over half of which was for March contracts in dollars and yen, while the smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw a low 428 million forints of trade, half of which was for March marks or dollars.
"The large number of March deals is mainly due to players closing their currently existing positions," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
Other traders said the dollar's sluggishness on the spot market encouraged a feeling that short-term dollar rates against the forint may fall.

The only other tangible trend was in the December Swiss franc, which traders still regard as a good long-term stable investment as they see Hungarian interest rates falling later in the year, Herczeg said.

On the BCE, the dollar fell for all months except December, with March dropping 34 fillers to 177.76, while the Swiss franc was steady for March to June but fell 29 fillers to 135.60 forints for December and by 1.15 forints to 139 forints for March 1998.
The central bank midday spot fix for the two currencies was 177.00 for the dollar and 119.98 for the Swiss franc.
Most of the turnover on the BSE, which trades only in the mark, dollar and Ecu, was taken up by agency crosses for March and December dollars, which accounted for three-quarters of all trade.
